strengths: Clear problem identification and motivation: distinguishes between storage and rendering memory compression, which is practical for edge devices
Strong empirical results: 8× static VRAM compression over vanilla 3DGS, 2× over SOTA (GaussianSpa) while maintaining comparable quality

Principled technical approach: memory-constrained optimization (Eq. 6) that naturally unifies primitive pruning and lobe pruning; ADMM-inspired solution handles non-differentiable constraints appropriately
Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple standard datasets, four categories of baseline comparisons, thorough ablation studies (Section 4.4) with clear improvements for each component
Insightful analysis of why compression-based methods fail (Table 2): explains why EAGLES/CompactGaussian paradoxically increase VRAM despite high storage compression

Well-motivated color representation choice: analytical comparison shows arbitrarily-oriented SG achieves comparable quality with half the parameters of 3rd-order SH and better represents local view-dependent signals
Elegant color compensation mechanism (Eq. 15): analytically derived to preserve energy of removed lobes, maintaining quality with smaller memory footprint
Practical impact demonstrated: enables real-time rendering on mobile devices (Figure 1) with interactive framerates
Clear presentation and visualization: well-structured paper with informative pipeline diagram (Figure 2) and qualitative results showing advantages on specular details
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: spherical gaussians already used in SG-Splatting (Wang et al., 2024b), unified pruning framework builds directly on GaussianSpa (Zhang et al., 2025b), primarily a novel combination of existing techniques

Incomplete joint optimization: proximal operator factorization (Eqs. 11-12) into separate projections for o and s may not guarantee optimality for the joint memory constraint, and optimality gap is not analyzed
Dynamic VRAM reduction not integrated into framework despite being part of the claimed '40% rendering VRAM reduction'—dynamic components depend on renderer implementation and remain unoptimized

Hyperparameter selection underspecified: budget κ selection strategy unclear, opacity threshold for post-processing not provided, number of fine-tuning steps unspecified, no sensitivity analysis for key parameters
Mixed quality results versus vanilla 3DGS: marginal improvement on Mip-NeRF360 (27.54 vs 27.48), slight degradation on Tanks&Temples (23.57 vs 23.68), only clear improvement on DeepBlending

Post-processing procedure is somewhat ad-hoc: two-stage approach with hard removal after soft optimization could be more principled; threshold for removing low-opacity primitives introduces additional undocumented hyperparameter
Limited scope of mobile device evaluation: Figure 1 shows only fps values without perceptual quality metrics; only qualitative evidence of mobile applicability

Representation choice not thoroughly justified: only compared against orthogonal-axis SG variant (~0.6dB gap could reflect optimization difficulty rather than representation limitation); no exploration of alternative compact representations
Reproducibility concerns: no code release mentioned, some implementation details missing, exact per-dataset hyperparameters not always specified

Limited failure case analysis: Section 5 acknowledges difficulty modeling 'particularly complex or intricate' highlights but does not provide experimental validation; no exploration of robustness to extreme material properties
